The All Progressives Congress and the All Progressives Grand Alliance are at loggerheads over the “progressives working together” mantra associated with the Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo. The phrase has become a recurring political theme in Anambra State, with Soludo presenting cooperation between APGA and the APC at the federal level as part of a broader progressive agenda. However, the Deputy National Chairman of the APC (South), Ben Nwoye, has rejected the claim that progressive forces are working together ahead of the 2027 general elections. Nwoye urged APC supporters not to be deceived by APGA’s “progressives are working together” slogan, describing the claim as a fallacy. Nwoye said the APC would work towards securing victory for its candidates in the 2027 elections, including President Bola Tinubu. The APC senatorial candidate for Anambra Central, Uche Ekwunife, said she and other party members were committed to securing support for the President and APC candidates in the state. Ekwunife, who is also the South-East Zonal Director of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said her interest and that of other APC candidates was to ensure the party performed strongly at the presidential, National Assembly and state assembly elections. ABUJA—The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to dismiss, as lacking in merit, the N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit that the former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, filed against him and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). The Inspector-General of Police was also listed as a respondent in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026. El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, dragged the respondents to court over an alleged unlawful raid on his Abuja residence. He specifically challenged the legality of the warrant the ICPC relied on to search his home. He prayed the court to declare that the search warrant dated February 4, which the Chief Magistrate of the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT signed to authorise the search and seizure of items from his residence, was invalid, null, and void. The former governor also sought a declaration that the search warrant was legally defective for lacking particularity, and for “material drafting errors, ambiguity in execution parameters, overbreadth, and absence of probable cause, thereby constituting an unlawful and unreasonable search in violation of Section 37 of the Constitution.” Other reliefs he sought include a declaration that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on February 19 at about 2 p.m., executed by agents of the ICPC and the Inspector-General of Police under the invalid warrant, “amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights to dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” The Chief Magistrate, who was initially listed as the 2nd respondent, was subsequently delisted from the case by the applicant. At the resumed proceedings on Monday, the AGF, through a lawyer from the Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Maimuna Lami-Shiru, notified the court of a counter-affidavit he had filed to challenge the competence of the suit. The AGF, among other things, contended that the former governor failed to disclose any reasonable cause of action to warrant the grant of the reliefs he is seeking from the court. While denying the allegation that the applicant’s rights were violated, the AGF insisted that both the ICPC and the IGP acted within the bounds of the law. He, therefore, urged the court to dismiss the suit. Meanwhile, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik adjourned the case until October 27 to allow El-Rufai’s lawyer, Akinyemi Aremu, to respond to the AGF’s counter-affidavit. The ICPC had earlier urged the court to dismiss the suit, insisting it acted on the strength of a petition that was filed against the former governor. The agency told the court that El-Rufai’s house was searched as part of its investigations into the petition, adding that its operatives acted with a valid search warrant issued on February 18. The commission said its officials were accompanied by police officers and that the search was conducted in the presence of the applicant’s wife, Hadiza El-Rufai, and his son, Mohammed El-Rufai. Likewise, the police, in their own counter-affidavit deposed to by Inspector Ewa Anthony, maintained that they had the statutory power to detect, arrest, investigate and prosecute offenders. The police told the court that their officers lawfully executed a search warrant that was issued by a competent court. El-Rufai currently faces multiple charges, including an allegation that he unlawfully intercepted the phone communications of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu. The ICPC had obtained court permission on March 12 to examine and analyse about 14 sets of electronic devices allegedly recovered when the former governor’s house was searched. Benue NBA urges Alia to sign retirement age bill for magistrates, law officers. The Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, branches in Makurdi, Gboko and Otukpo have appealed to Benue State Governor Hyacinth Alia to approve legislation seeking to extend the retirement age of magistrates and law officers in the state Ministry of Justice. The branches said the bill, which was passed by the Benue State House of Assembly on May 6, 2026, would help preserve the expertise of experienced legal practitioners within the state’s justice system. Chairman of the Makurdi NBA Branch, Joseph Mtemdoo Gbagyo, made the appeal while speaking on behalf of the three branches at the opening of the 2026/2027 Benue State Judiciary Legal Year at the High Court Complex in Makurdi. The event was held under the theme: “The Nigerian Judiciary at a Crossroads: Innovations, Accountability and Public Trust.” Gbagyo explained that the annual Legal Year ceremony provides an opportunity for legal professionals to review developments within the justice sector and identify priorities for the new year. He also highlighted other legislation passed by the Assembly, including the Area Court Amendment Law 2026, subject to confirmation by the Chief Judge, alongside laws establishing the State Electricity Commission and the Water and Sanitation Regulatory Commission. The NBA chairman conveyed goodwill from the 33rd President of the association, Mrs Oyinkansola Badejo-Okunsanya, SAN, who recently reiterated her commitment to improving relations between the Bar and the Bench through constructive engagement. Gbagyo commended Chief Judge Justice Maurice Ahemba Ikpambese for his leadership and efforts to improve court infrastructure, digitalise operations and expand magisterial divisions across the state. He identified renovation works at courts in Daudu, Tarka, Adikpo, Okpoga and Makurdi as notable steps towards improving working conditions for judicial personnel. The chairman further acknowledged the establishment of a health clinic at the High Court Complex for judiciary staff and lawyers, as well as initiatives promoting gender inclusion and the protection of vulnerable groups. He welcomed plans to revive quarterly Bar-Bench meetings, describing the engagement as an avenue for addressing challenges affecting the administration of justice. Gbagyo also appreciated Governor Alia for granting financial autonomy to the state judiciary and supporting infrastructure projects, including the construction of a new Ministry of Justice Complex and the harmonisation of the salary structure for members of the Law Officers Association of Nigeria (LOAN). However, he urged the governor to approve robe allowances for law officers. The NBA chairman also praised the appointment of lawyers to strategic government positions, including Secretary to the State Government, Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Chief of Staff to the Governor, and Principal Special Assistant on Legal Matters.

2027: We don’t trust INEC to protect our votes – ADC. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, says it does not trust the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to protect its votes in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. The National Publicity Secretary of the party, Bolaji Abdullahi, made this statement on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today. According to him, the party is making arrangements to collate its votes, warning that INEC’s technical failures undermine trust. “Don’t forget that I ran for Senate in the 2023 election. What many of us did, and not only myself, was that we trusted INEC when they told us there would be automatic transmission of results to the IReV. “Then what happened afterwards? They said that, due to some technical glitch, the results could not be transmitted automatically to the IReV. So we have been beaten by that, and we are now twice shy. We say we will not allow it to happen again. We are no longer naive. “We can no longer trust INEC to protect our votes for us. We are saying that we will vigilantly guard our own votes. We will protect our own votes. “If the results at the end of the day reflect the true votes that came from the polling units, we will accept them. But if they do not, we are not going to accept them. We are making provisions to collate our own votes,” he said.

Why we stopped Peter Obi from winning Rivers in 2023 – Wike. Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has opened up on the circumstances surrounding Peter Obi’s failure to win the 2023 presidential election in Rivers State. DAILY POST reports that there have been allegations that the outcome of the polls, particularly in Rivers State, was manipulated to favour the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. Peter Obi, who was the presidential flagbearer of the Labour Party in the last election, had instead claimed that he won the election in Rivers State. Speaking during an interview on TVC News on Monday, Wike said he and members of the defunct G-5 governors stopped Peter Obi from winning the state. According to him, the Labour Party was allowed to win parts of the South-South in the 2023 elections to prevent the then-presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Atiku Abubakar, from winning the region. He said, “We in the G-5 have our strategy. We said the PDP was stronger in the South-South and our problem was Atiku. Therefore, instead of Atiku taking it, let it go to the Labour Party. “It was only Rivers State where we said, ‘No, we have a problem here in Rivers. Obi will not win here. If he wins, he will send a signal somewhere.’ We stopped it. “It is no longer the same scenario. I can tell you authoritatively now that Obi can’t win the South-South.”

2027: No amount of solo effort will make someone from Southeast become president – Anyim. A former President of the Nigerian Senate, Anyim Pius Anyim, has said that nobody from the Southeast will become President of Nigeria without an alliance with other regions. Anyim said this was the reason he left the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, to join the All Progressives Congress, APC. Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Anyim is one of the Southeast politicians who have joined the ruling party and declared their support for President Bola Tinubu’s second term. The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, from the Southeast, is one of the most popular contenders in the forthcoming presidential election. However, Anyim believes that the region should wait until the next 12 years, when the zoning arrangement will return to the South. He told Arise News: “The President is entitled to a second term; after his term, the rotation goes to the North, and then it will come to the Southeast. You need to support others so they will support you.” Speaking further, Anyim said: “Before I joined APC, you would ask me why APC. I weighed the fact that when we worked together, I mean the aspirants, our primary interest was our zone. “So, in choosing which party to go to, I had to weigh the party that would serve that primary interest. The experience we gathered from that process, from that context, the experience I personally gathered, is that no person from the Southeast would make it in isolation. “We must have an alliance with other regions in order to make it. So, there is no amount of effort from each and every one of us that will make it possible for us to become president if we do not have an alliance with other regions. “It is the same thing with every other region. So, I now decided that, look, APC is best serving that interest, and when I considered that APC would serve that interest better, I joined APC. “The President has taken it from the Southwest. After his second term, I believe in rotation. Of course, it will go to the North. Then, after the North, it will come down. In other words, after eight years, it will come down to the Southeast.”

UNGA: Tinubu sitting side by side with Trump wouldn’t make any difference – Pius Anyim. Former Senate President, Anyim Pius Anyim, has noted that the arrangement for President Bola Tinubu to sit side by side with US President Donald Trump at the United Nations General Assembly, UNGA, would not have made any difference. He argued that no meaningful discussion would have emerged from such a seating arrangement, since the US leader would have had his schedule for the event set a year ahead. Anyim said President Tinubu’s absence from the event should not be an issue, adding that Nigerians are aware that their leader is currently on leave. He also noted that Vice President Kashim Shettima is in charge in the absence of the President and has been assigned to represent Nigeria at the UNGA. Anyim said he does not understand why there is so much noise about the President’s absence from the UNGA, adding that there is nothing that compels the President to attend the General Assembly. Speaking on Arise News, the former Senate President said, “I don’t understand why his absence should be an issue, but I think Nigerians are aware; they very well know that the President is on a short vacation. “And his vice is in charge while he is away, and he simply assigns his vice to undertake the assignment. I don’t know why we are making so much out of this. Well, there is nothing that compels the President to be at UNGA. The Vice President can represent the country, even the Foreign Minister.” Asked what kind of message the President’s decision could be sending to the rest of Africa, and indeed the world, having missed the UN General Assembly for the third time in his nearly four years in office, Anyim added, “The structure of UNGA is the General Assembly and side meetings. “Side meetings could be bilateral; side meetings could be a little multilateral and all that. And what is it in that General Assembly statement? It is simply to read the statement from your country. Is this something that the Vice President cannot do? “If the President did not schedule side meetings, and it’s only to appear in the General Assembly to present a statement, I don’t know what he [Tinubu] is losing. So, except if there are side meetings that were scheduled and he is not able to attend those side meetings.” On the plan that President Tinubu was going to be sitting next to US President Donald Trump, Anyim said, “We don’t take any president by chance. The fact that you sit together with President [Trump] doesn’t make any difference. “The President of America normally would have his schedules a year ahead. So, I don’t see the reason for all the whole fuss about the presence at UNGA and not being present at UNGA.”

Rainbow Coalition: APC needs Wike more, he has qualities like Tinubu – Jibrin. House of Representatives member representing Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency, Hon. Abdulmumin Jibrin, has told the Progressive Governors Forum, PGF, that the All Progressives Congress, APC, needs the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, more than the former Rivers State governor needs the ruling party. He also pointed out that other political parties, such as the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, are waiting for the opportunity to take Wike into their folds should he decide not to work with the APC again. He said the APC governors should negotiate with the Minister, just as President Bola Tinubu did. The Progressive Governors’ Forum, led by the Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, is strongly opposed to the Rainbow Coalition, which now stands as a clear threat to the governors and their candidates across the states ahead of the upcoming general elections. The list recently published by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, indicates that Wike’s Rainbow Coalition has over 100 senatorial candidates and many more other positions, such as the House of Representatives and State Assemblies. Speaking on Arise News on Monday evening, Jibrin, a chieftain of the APC, pointed out that Wike has worked much more than expected for the ruling party and must not be allowed to leave at this point when the President still needs him for the upcoming election. “Somebody like Wike will continue to be Wike in and out of office. He has qualities like the President. The President today— you take him out as the President, he would still continue to maintain his relevance. “After all, he was out of office for 16, 17 years, and his relevance was intact. Wike is that sort of a person, so Wike will be in demand all the time. “For the fact that we had Wike in 2023, there is no need for any renewal. Automatically, for goodness’ sake, APC needs Wike, and I just want to be a bit subtle; I would have said much more than he needs us. “Because today, if he pulls out of the APC, he’ll be in high demand all over the country, and that’s why I’ve been saying, let our governors— I love our governors; some of them weren’t happy about my intervention, but I took time to explain to them that, look, what you need to do with Wike is to negotiate with Wike. “If the President of the country hadn’t negotiated with Wike and brought Wike on board today, there would have been a Rainbow Coalition in this country against APC. So, if the President will understand that, let me negotiate with this man because he has value, he has something to bring to the table, governors should follow suit. “You just have to approach it in a pragmatic manner, and you see, the cases of the states are different. They are not the same. They are not uniform. That was why I was shocked. I’m choosing my words carefully. I don’t want the governors to say I’m hard on them. “My relationship with them is intact. But I believe that the models they adopted by going to do the press conference just to hit hard on Wike—I believe that it’s wrong because all the states, their cases are peculiar; they’re different cases, and there’s nothing wrong with going into discussion with Wike. “Anything that I see can pose a danger to the re-election of the President, I will always intervene.”

The West has different laws to describe situations that society cannot explain. Electoral Integrity and Political Neutrality State Police will inevitably play important roles during elections. Given the heightened political tensions that often accompany electoral periods, the National Policing Bill should establish safeguards to protect electoral integrity and prevent partisan abuse. Operational independence during elections; Mandatory coordination with INEC and other security agencies; and Independent monitoring of election-related policing activities. Additional measures should include documented deployment decisions, public reporting on election security operations and sanctions for officers or political actors who misuse policing powers for partisan purposes. State Police must never become instruments for intimidating voters, harassing opposition parties or restricting lawful political activity. Their role is to protect the electoral process, safeguard voters and maintain public order impartially. Democratic legitimacy requires political neutrality. IX. Fiscal Sustainability, Weapons Management and State Readiness Certification No policing institution can function effectively without sustainable financing. States seeking to establish police services should demonstrate the capacity to: Security institutions should be established on the basis of demonstrated fiscal capacity rather than political aspiration. The National Policing Bill should also establish: Given existing concerns regarding the proliferation of small arms and light weapons, strict weapons management standards are essential. The Bill should further establish a State Readiness Certification Framework. Before commencing operations, a state should demonstrate minimum capacity in fiscal sustainability, human resource management, training infrastructure, independent complaints mechanisms, legislative oversight, digital records management, armoury controls and diversity safeguards. Institutional readiness should precede operational authority. The transition from a unitary policing structure to a dual policing system should be gradual, sequenced and carefully managed. Even well-designed reforms can fail if implementation is rushed or poorly coordinated. The National Policing Bill should provide for: A national transition oversight mechanism should monitor implementation, identify emerging challenges and recommend corrective actions. The movement of personnel, assets and operational responsibilities must be carefully coordinated to avoid service disruptions, duplication and security gaps. A phased approach will allow lessons from early implementation to inform broader rollout. The State Police debate is often presented as a choice between centralisation and decentralisation. That framing is inadequate. The real choice before Nigeria is between institution-based policing and power-based policing. Neither centralisation nor decentralisation guarantees effectiveness, accountability or public trust. Success depends on the quality of the institutions that govern policing power. State Police can strengthen public safety, improve local responsiveness and deepen federalism. It can also become vulnerable to political capture, identity-based exclusion and institutional fragmentation. The outcome will depend on the constitutional safeguards, governance institutions and accountability mechanisms established today. The decentralisation of policing must not become the decentralisation of impunity. Rather, it should become an opportunity to build more responsive, professional and citizen-centred security institutions. Tinubu warns police against political bias ahead of 2027 elections By Jide Olusola President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has charged the Nigeria Police Force to maintain strict political neutrality and the highest standards of professionalism ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that the Force must not be perceived as serving any political interest. Tinubu gave the charge at the 2026 Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers in Owerri, Imo State, in an address delivered on his behalf by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume. The President said every Nigerian, regardless of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion, social status or geographical location, must feel protected by the police, stressing that the Force’s neutrality would be critical to public confidence in the electoral process. “The police must be seen not as an instrument of any political interest, but as a national institution serving the Nigerian people and protecting the constitutional order. This is fundamental to public trust and to the credibility of our democracy”, the President said. Speaking on the theme, “Developing a Nigeria Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections”, Tinubu said the 2027 elections would require careful preparation, intelligence-led operations, professionalism, impartiality and effective coordination among security and electoral stakeholders. He said securing elections goes beyond protecting polling stations and ballot materials, noting that the police must also protect citizens and electoral officials, ensure peaceful campaigns, prevent violence and intimidation, and guarantee that Nigerians can participate without fear. Tinubu reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to police reforms, saying sustained investment in personnel, training, technology, intelligence infrastructure, operational logistics, welfare and institutional systems remained necessary. He urged the Force to strengthen intelligence gathering, improve response times, deepen community engagement, embrace technology and enhance inter-agency cooperation in confronting increasingly sophisticated security threats. The President commended Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and the Police Management Team for efforts to reposition the Force and tackle emerging security challenges. He also acknowledged officers confronting kidnapping, terrorism, banditry, armed robbery, cultism and other violent crimes, including those who had paid the ultimate price. Tinubu urged senior officers to use the retreat to develop a practical roadmap for election security and operational preparedness, while building a modern, professional, technology-enabled, intelligence-driven and citizen-centred police force beyond 2027. He said Federal Government support for the police must be matched by courage, integrity, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their constitutional responsibilities. Nigeria records first tele-robotic surgery in West Africa. Nisa Premier Hospital, Abuja, has partnered with RoboMed Global and The Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) to successfully perform what the hospital described as the first tele-robotic surgery in Nigeria and West Africa. The landmark kidney cancer surgery was performed on a patient at Nisa Premier Hospital, Abuja, while the surgeon, Professor Obi Ekwenna-Davis, remotely controlled the robotic surgical platform from Redeemer’s Health Village in Lagos. The procedure, which lasted approximately three hours, was performed to remove a kidney affected by a cancerous tumour. The hospital said the patient had been discharged following the successful procedure, although details about the patient’s identity and condition were withheld for privacy reasons. Speaking during an event to mark the milestone, the Chief Executive Officer of Nisa Premier Hospital, Dr Ibrahim Wada, said the development demonstrated the potential of tele-robotic surgery to connect specialist surgical expertise with patients across Nigeria. Wada said the procedure was carried out using the MicroPort robotic surgical platform installed at Nisa Premier Hospital, with the remote surgeon controlling the system from Lagos. He said the development could reduce the need for Nigerians to travel abroad for specialised medical treatment, thereby reducing expenditure on international travel, accommodation and medical services. According to him, the technology also creates an opportunity for Nigerians to access specialised expertise from doctors located in other parts of the world without requiring the doctors to travel physically to Nigeria. “This exemplifies one of the positive areas of diaspora and home collaboration,” Wada said. He added that the development would allow Nigerian doctors to continue receiving training and build capacity in robotic surgery, while creating opportunities for international experts to collaborate with local medical teams. Explaining the advantages of robotic surgery, Wada said the technology could reduce the size of surgical incisions and shorten patients’ recovery periods compared with conventional open surgery. He said patients undergoing major procedures could potentially be discharged the same day or within 24 hours, depending on the nature of the surgery and the doctor’s assessment, instead of spending several days in hospital. Wada also said robotic systems could provide greater precision during surgery because the instruments are controlled through a robotic platform. He, however, stressed that patient safety remained a major consideration, particularly because telesurgery depends heavily on stable and secure communication networks. “Machinery can go wrong. Connections can cease. So we always make sure there is a team on the ground that can do the needful and take over the robot locally, if necessary,” he said. He compared the arrangement to the aviation industry, where automated systems are used, but pilots remain available to intervene when necessary. Wada said the telesurgery required a dedicated and highly secure internet connection capable of supporting communication between the robotic systems in Abuja and Lagos. He explained that the network requirements were significantly more complex than ordinary internet connections used for phones and computers. He said the first procedure experienced some delay due to connectivity issues, but the technical team eventually established the required connection. According to him, the experience showed the need for further testing, stronger infrastructure and continuous improvement of the technology before it can be widely deployed. Leaders of 15 political parties in Kaduna State have condemned the recent attack on the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Isa Mohammed Ashiru. According to the statement, leaders of the political parties paid a solidarity visit to Ashiru at his Kaduna residence following the attack on him and members of his entourage. Adubi noted that the party leaders expressed grave concern during the visit over what they described as rising incidents of political intimidation and violence across the state. He quoted the coalition as emphasizing that political disagreements must not degenerate into attacks, harassment, or threats against opponents. The leaders stressed that political parties and candidates possess the constitutional right to organize meetings, hold rallies, engage supporters, and canvass for votes without fear of intimidation or physical violence. They urged political actors, party supporters, and relevant authorities to promote peace, tolerance, and respect for the rule of law ahead of the 2027 polls. The party leaders also commended Ashiru for remaining calm and steadfast in his commitment to the democratic process despite the provocation. Responding, Ashiru thanked the visiting delegation for their solidarity and concern, assuring them that the incident would not deter him or his supporters from pursuing their political aspirations through peaceful and lawful means. He reiterated his commitment to running an issues-based campaign centered on the development and welfare of the people of Kaduna State. “Political competition should be about ideas, policies, and programs rather than violence and intimidation,” Ashiru stated. Is Tinubu above the law?. President Bola Tinubu left Abuja for London on August 30, this time for a three week “working vacation.” Vice President Kashim Shettima was in Angola at the time, representing him at an African Union summit. Two of Nigeria’s most powerful officials, outside the country simultaneously, and no letter to the National Assembly. That is the story in one sentence. Everything else is commentary. Section 145 of the 1999 Constitution is not ambiguous. It says that whenever the president transmits a written declaration to the Senate President and the Speaker that he is proceeding on vacation or is otherwise unable to discharge his duties, the vice president shall perform those functions as acting president until the president transmits a written declaration to the contrary. It is a simple mechanism. Buhari used it routinely. Tinubu, since May 2023, has not used it once. Should this surprise anyone who watched Tinubu govern Lagos? It should not. Ask Kofoworola Bucknor-Akerele, his first deputy governor, who resigned in 2002 after concluding that he had no intention of sharing authority with her. She has said, in more than one interview since, that he wanted control of the party machinery and would not be checked by anyone, including the woman elected to stand beside him. That is not gossip. That is a documented pattern stretching back a quarter of a century, and it did not end when he moved from Alausa to Aso Rock. So when Bayo Onanuga, the president’s spokesman, announces a vacation and says nothing about who is minding the republic, is that an oversight? Is it discretion? Or is it a governing philosophy, one in which power is personal property rather than a public trust that can be lent, even briefly, to the man a duly elected president chose as his own running mate? Section 145 is not an isolated lapse. It fits a wider pattern under this administration: appointments made with little regard for constitutional procedure, contracts awarded with little regard for due process. The question this raises is larger than one clause of the constitution. Why should a president continue to behave as though he is above the law, not through one dramatic act, but through a steady accumulation of small refusals to be bound by the rules everyone else must observe? Consider what the president is actually saying, by his silence on Section 145. He is saying that Shettima, the man he handpicked and is running with again for a second term, cannot be trusted to sign a file for three weeks. He is saying that a written declaration to the Senate President, a two paragraph formality that Buhari managed without incident, is somehow beneath this vacation or beyond it. Which is it? Nigerians deserve an answer, not a press statement that talks about London hotels and says nothing about Section 145. Compare this to Buhari, whatever else one thinks of his presidency. Buhari transmitted power to Osinbajo for medical trips, Hajj travel, and routine absences, several times across eight years. Nobody confused Osinbajo for a co-president. Those handovers were unremarkable precisely because they were lawful and expected. That is what a functioning transfer mechanism looks like. It disappears into the routine of governance. It does not become news. Under Tinubu, the absence of a handover has become news, again and again, because the presidency keeps declining to explain it. Atiku Abubakar called the situation a “disturbing vacuum of political leadership,” and for once the opposition’s criticism understates the problem rather than exaggerating it. This is not simply about who answers the phone if a crisis erupts while both men are abroad. This is about whether the officeholder respects the document that put him there, in the small matters as much as the large ones. Here is the deeper question the political class in Abuja seems unwilling to ask aloud. Tinubu extends vacation abroad, announces return. President Tinubu will return to Nigeria at the weekend, following the extension of his working vacation by a few days. President Tinubu departed Nigeria on 30 August for London to begin the working vacation. After spending a week in London, he moved to Paris, France, where he met with French President Emmanuel Macron and businessman Mr Vincent Bollore, whose media group includes Canal+, Multichoice, and Universal Music Group. Since he began the vacation, President Tinubu has continued to keep in touch with home, directing the affairs of the nation, like ordering an independent panel to investigate the death of 37 illegal miners in Minna, following their detention by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, among other things. While away, President Tinubu delegated Vice President Kashim Shettima to represent him at some official functions. Though Mr Shettima left Abuja on 20 September for New York to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, who has also been representing the president at events, will continue to do so. On the political front, the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Abubakar Yari, has been leading notable party leaders in consultations with prominent traditional rulers in the country. The presidency described the baseless insinuation by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and a United States-based lobbying firm headed by an ex-convict about President Tinubu’s non-attendance at UNGA as irresponsible. Italiya na shirin haramtawa mata sanya niƙabi a makarantu. Firaministar Italiya Giorgia Meloni ta ce gwamnatin ƙasar na shirin haramta amfani da niƙabi ko duk wani nau’in kyallen rufe fuska ga mata a makarantu, tare da sanya iyaka kan adadin ɗaliban ƙasashen waje da za su kasance a aji guda. Meloni ta bayyana hakan ne a ranar Lahadi yayin wani taro na matasan jam’iyyarta ta Brothers of Italy. Ta ce nan ba da daɗewa ba za a gabatar da wani ƙudiri a gaban majalisar ministoci domin kafa dokar da za ta ƙayyade adadin ɗaliban ƙasashen waje da za a bari su kasance a aji guda. Ta kuma ce ƙudirin zai buƙaci iyayen ɗaliban ƙasashen waje da ke fuskantar matsalar sabawa da tsarin makarantu su koyi harshen Italiyanci. A cewar Meloni, ƙudirin zai kuma haramta amfani da niƙabi a makarantu. A halin yanzu, babu wata doka kai tsaye a Italiya da ta haramta niƙabi a makarantu ko wuraren taruwar jama’a. Sai dai wata doka ta shekarar 1975 ta haramta amfani da hular kariya ko tufafin da ke hana gano fuskar mutum, sai dai idan akwai dalili na musamman. A shekarar 2008, wata babbar kotu a Italiya ta bayyana cewa ana iya sanya mayafin da ke rufe fuska saboda dalilai na addini ko al'adu, matuƙar za a bayyana fuskar lokacin da ake buƙatar tabbatar da shaida mutum. Dangane da adadin ɗaliban ƙasashen waje a aji guda kuwa, wannan iyaka tuni tana cikin dokokin Italiya, amma Meloni ba ta bayyana yadda sabuwar dokar za ta sauya tsarin wadda ake amfani da ita ba. Tun daga shekarar 2010, dokar Italiya ta kayyade cewa daliban ƙasashen waje ba za su wuce kaso 30 cikin 100 na yawan ɗalibai a aji guda ko na makaranta ba. Sai dai ana iya ƙara wannan kaso idan ɗaliban ƙasashen waje suna da isasshen ƙwarewa a harshen Italiyanci, kamar waɗanda aka haifa a Italiya, haka kuma, ana iya rage adadin idan ɗaliban ba su iya harshen Italiyanci yadda ya kamata ba. The improvement in security was phenomenal, such that the former IG of Police (Abubakar Mohammed) lauded Anambra State for not witnessing any bank robbery in my last three years in office. 21. Modified: 5:24am On Sep 20 APC’s Yakubu Ali Wins Disina Bye-Election by Deborah Akwa September 20, 2026 The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Yakubu Ali, has won the Disina State Constituency by-election in Bauchi State. The election was held on Saturday across 95 polling units in Disina Constituency, with results announced on Sunday. Ali polled 5,846 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Babangida Isaq of the All Progressives Movement (APM), who scored 5,225 votes. Ali won by 621 votes. The Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) candidate, Alhaji Rilwanu Galadiman Disina, finished third with 3,701 votes. The constituency is in Shira Local Government Area of Bauchi State. The bye-election drew candidates from the APC, APM and PRP, among other political interests. Before the poll,  People’s Redemption Party (PRP) leaders had called for a peaceful and credible election. They also urged political parties and their supporters to avoid violence, intimidation and inflammatory statements. The PRP had presented Rilwanu Galadiman Disina as its candidate during its campaign in the constituency. During the campaign, PRP governorship candidate Senator Shehu Buba Umar urged political actors to focus on issues, leadership and service rather than personal attacks. The Disina election was one of the State Assembly by-elections. With 5,846 votes, Ali emerged before Isaq and Galadiman Disina to secure the Disina State Constituency seat. ‘It’s not APC’s fault PDP didn’t zone presidency to South-East’ — Anyim. Former Senate President Pius Anyim Pius has said the All Progressives Congress, APC, should not be blamed for the failure of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, to zone its presidential ticket to the South-East in previous election cycles. Anyim said the decision was informed partly by his belief that the South-East could only produce a president through alliances with other regions. He spoke on Arise TV’s Prime Time on Monday while discussing the zoning arrangement that has eluded the South-East since the return to democratic rule in 1999. The former Senate president said his political experience had convinced him that no South-East presidential candidate could succeed by relying solely on support from the region. “If PDP had been honorable enough to zone to the South-East, it would have stimulated the necessary sentiments that will help us defeat any other candidate. “And in the eyes and minds of the north, the rotation applied because it’s still in the south and so there is nothing to blame anybody about,” he said. Anyim said the South-East should instead focus on building political alliances with other regions to improve its chances of producing the president. He said this consideration influenced his decision to join the APC after spending about a year weighing his options. “It took me about a year to join the APC. But then you will ask me why APC? I weighed the fact that when we worked together, I mean the aspirants, our primary interest was our zone,” he said. He added that he chose the APC after concluding that the party could better serve the South-East’s long-term political interest. “The experience I personally gathered is that no person from the South-East would make it in isolation. We must have an alliance with other regions in order to make it,” Anyim said. He argued that the region’s political strategy should therefore involve supporting other regions when necessary to secure reciprocal support in the future. “There is no amount of effort from each and every one of us that will make it possible for us to become president, if we do not have an alliance with other regions,” he said. On the current zoning arrangement, Anyim acknowledged that President Bola Tinubu had secured the presidency for the South-West and said he was entitled to seek a second term. “Certainly the president had taken it for the southwest, and he’s entitled to a second term. So, after his second term, I believe in rotation. Of course, it will go to the north. Then after the north, it will come down,” he said. Anyim said the South-East would need to continue building relationships with other parts of the country rather than pursuing the presidency in isolation. “But you need to support others so that they can support you,” he added. All my children supported Peter Obi in 2023 – Wike. Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has revealed that all his children supported Peter Obi, the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, during the 2023 presidential election. Wike disclosed this on Monday during an interview on TVC News. The former Rivers State governor, however, attributed their support for Obi to the controversy surrounding the All Progressives Congress, APC, Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket during the 2023 election. He said the situation had changed, claiming that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had addressed the concerns surrounding the same-faith ticket. “In 2023, there was a problem with the Muslim-Muslim ticket. There was this campaign about Christianity. “All my children supported Peter Obi. But now, they are saying that they never knew this man, Peter Obi, was like this. “There are a lot of people who were carried away, but that is no longer there now. Tinubu has been able to kill the Muslim-Muslim ticket problem,” Wike said. Wike further insisted that Obi, who is now the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, cannot win the 2027 presidential election.

Operation intelligence-driven – Dikko on killing of 18 bandits in Katsina. Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, has commended the military, Department of State Services (DSS) and local vigilantes for foiling a planned mass kidnapping in Bakori Local Government Area and neutralising 18 armed bandits. The operation took place at about 1am on Monday, September 21, 2026, at Gidan Iyado in Kakumi Ward, according to the state Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs. The ministry said the joint operation involved hunters, members of the Community Watch Corps and local vigilante groups, who ambushed the bandits following intelligence about a planned mass abduction for ransom. The state Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Nasir Mua’su, said the operation was intelligence-driven and targeted a group allegedly terrorising Kakumi Ward and neighbouring communities. “The operation was intelligence-driven. Acting on credible information about planned mass abduction for ransom by the criminal group, our forces laid ambush using operational assets and engaged the bandits.” The commissioner identified the alleged leader of the group as Alhaji Musa Duki, a former school headmaster who reportedly became a bandit kingpin operating from Mununu Forest in Faskari Local Government Area. Security forces recovered one G3 rifle, two AK-47 rifles, 14 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition and three motorcycles during the operation. They also recovered two cows and 94 sheep believed to have been rustled by the criminals. Mua’su said Governor Radda praised the security personnel for their gallantry and assured residents that operations would continue to dismantle the criminal network. “A sustained covert operation is ongoing to track and neutralize the kingpin and dismantle his network completely. We will not relent until every forest and hideout is cleared.” He added that the military and DSS were working to identify other members of the network, locate their hideouts and prevent further kidnapping attacks in Bakori, Faskari and neighbouring communities. The state government described the operation as a major breakthrough in its ongoing efforts to tackle banditry and protect communities across Katsina State.
